summary.text: A 67-year-old woman with a history of atrial fibrillation and hyperlipidemia, and no prior seizure, dementia or neuro-psychiatric disorder, received 17D yellow fever and hepatitis B vaccines before planned travel to Guyana. Two weeks later she developed dizziness, double vision, sore throat and low-grade fever, and five weeks after that she presented to an outside hospital with disequilibrium, diplopia and numbness.

Outside-hospital CT, MRI, MRA, EEG and routine labs were unremarkable apart from non-specific white matter changes, and a lumbar puncture showed mildly elevated protein. She was discharged, was found aphasic three days later, was discharged with concern for a functional neurologic disorder, and returned with persistent aphasia, hypoxia and secretions requiring intubation, levetiracetam and propofol before transfer for status epilepticus.

On NSICU admission she was comatose with hyper-reflexia, clonus and up-going toes. MRI showed gray matter diffusion restriction raising concern for prion disease, with EEG periodic discharges and lymphocytic pleocytosis. Empiric IVIG was started and stopped after three treatments. CSF 14-3-3 was positive, a negative RT-QuIC ruled out vCJD, CSF and serum neutralization titers were 1:256 and 1:640, and the authors confirmed YEL-AND. NSICU complications included urinary tract infection and bacteremia.

MRI abnormalities largely resolved by hospital day 16 and fully resolved at 3 months. Recovery was complicated by dysphagia, urinary retention and apathy; she left for inpatient rehabilitation with a MoCA of 7/30. Post-infectious parkinsonism was diagnosed at follow-up and treated with levodopa-carbidopa, with improvement, return home, weaning of anti-epileptic therapy and repeat MoCA above 20.
